Very nice and very helpful!

For any other TMB newbies, I ran into a little problem on my Mac with simpleExample, though, loading the DLL--got a message saying "could not find path-to-working-directory/simpleExample". Don't know if you'd run into the same trouble on Windows.

Looking at one of the other examples, the solution was to change 'dyn.load("simpleExample")' to 'dyn.load(dynlib("simpleExample"))'

Cheers,

Buck

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] dbinom_robut for logistic regression
messages.body_plain:
There are a few problems I can see.

(1)
Maybe I don’t understand the big picture of your model, but the order of calculations seems weird. I’m assuming X1 and Y are data; a and b are parameters. You should probably have this line

> LogitP(i) = a + b*X1(i);

before this one
> P(i) = inv_logit(LogitP(i));
you might not even need this second one (see next comment).

(2)
This line seems strange Y_hat(i) = max(Type(0), min(Type(1),P(i)));
Shouldn’t P(i) always be between 0 and 1? If so, won’t this calculation always make Y_hat(i)=P(i)?
If there is a reason to do this in the model, there’s still a risk that using max and min will cause discontinuities in the likelihood surface.

(3)
dbinom_robust takes these arguments
dbinom_robust(Type k, Type size, Type logit_p, int give_log=0)
In the case of Bernoulli data, size =1, but you’ll need to use Type(1).)

Maybe you just need

> LogitP(i) = a + b*X1(i);

> nll-= dbinom_robust(Y(i),Type(1),LogitP(i),true);
